answer: An agent economy can weight each identity’s voting power by the funds it locks in escrow, with a 30-day withdrawal delay. Fake accounts may branch like a vine, but splitting one deposit among them creates no extra voting power. The public escrow ledger serves as a lantern: every vote traces to locked capital. To control a majority, an attacker must lock more funds than honest voters combined, making a spiral of new identities useless without fresh capital.
